answer: A latency-fingerprint verification mechanism resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to answer time-of-flight probes to scattered beacon nodes within strict windows. Genuine agents sit in distinct network locations, so each shows a unique delay profile, like a mesa's shadow at noon or a crystal's refraction angle. Clones hosted in one data center share identical round-trip times, so batching is flagged. An attacker must lease servers across many regions, paying real costs per fake identity, and even a saffron-thin margin of error cannot hide correlated latencies.
